card.name: Lakhon Khol
card.era: Roots in the Angkor/pre-Angkorian era; UNESCO-listed 2018
card.tagline: All-male Khmer masked theatre of the Reamker
card.profile: Lakhon Khol is a Cambodian masked dance-drama performed by men wearing elaborate painted masks, accompanied by a pinpeat orchestra and melodious recitation, enacting episodes of the Reamker (the Khmer Ramayana) with the four character types neang, neayrong, yeak (giant) and sva (monkey) (Wikipedia; UNESCO). At Wat Svay Andet near Phnom Penh it is performed for ritual purposes linked to rice farming, with spirit mediums facilitating interactions between the Neak Ta guardian spirits, performers and villagers.
card.insight: Lkhon Khol Wat Svay Andet was inscribed on UNESCO's List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in Need of Urgent Safeguarding on November 28, 2018 (13.COM, Port Louis, Mauritius); the tradition nearly vanished under the Khmer Rouge, surviving through a handful of masters who passed it to a new generation (Wikipedia; Bangkok Post).
